taxonomic_note: Species-level learner target. Do not assign variety without exact specimen/source support.
look_here_first: Start at the flower head, then move straight to the calyx. Purple prairie clover forms dense thimble-like to cylindrical heads; for the difficult D. purpurea versus D. compacta split, use calyx pubescence rather than flower color.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 24-county boundary audit 2026-10-14: Concho, Tom Green qualify; Bell out-of-zone and excluded from PASS. Previous evidence preserved in range_audit; third approved county pending.

range_audit.rule_source: PROJECT_RULES.md — Target zone and minimum three native counties

best_field_traits: perennial with stiff upright stems from a deep root
alternate odd-pinnate leaves with usually 3–7 very narrow leaflets
dense thimble-shaped to cylindrical terminal flower heads
flowers progress upward on the head
small legume with one or two seeds
calyx pubescence pattern is a priority character versus Dalea compacta
morphology_keys.comparison_training: D. compacta is the priority confuser: D. compacta has calyx hairs arranged in longitudinal lines separated by bald areas, while D. purpurea has hairs distributed over the calyx-tube surface. D. enneandra has a loose spike with exposed rachis; D. tenuis is consistently 3-foliolate with extremely narrow leaflets.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Do not identify primarily by purple flower color. Use calyx pubescence versus D. compacta, spike density versus D. enneandra, and leaflet number/width versus D. tenuis.

photo_strategy.visual_priority: habit + leaf architecture + flower-head progression + calyx macro
photo_strategy.remaining_need: Add a clear calyx macro/annotated comparison versus D. compacta when available.
